tonight.headline: Waivers process at 01:00 tonight. Two claims to file before then.
body: Nothing has kicked off. Week 3 starts Thursday evening with Atlanta at Green Bay, and your first player does not play until Sunday at 11:00 — Kyle Pitts on Thursday is the exception, and he is on your bench.

So the only thing that expires tonight is the waiver board. Every one of the 119 available players in Chem is on waivers clearing at 07:00 UTC, which is 01:00 Wednesday here. Priority resets weekly in this league and you are 2nd of 10, so the claims below cost you nothing beyond the roster seat. File them and go to bed; the Coker lineup change can wait until Sunday morning.

case.label: Why you are favoured
case.body: ESPN projects AVIATO 128.1 to Footballers' 104.2, a 62% win probability. The gap is almost entirely their quarterback: Caleb Williams is in their starting slot projecting 0.0, with a hamstring that Ben Johnson said on Monday will keep him out of practice all week. They have no second quarterback.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Brock Bowers. Schefter said on 22 September he would be surprised if Bowers were not back this week after his pre-Week-1 meniscus procedure. Footballers start him at tight end and he has played nothing yet, so his 14.2 is the softest number on their sheet in both directions. Jaxon Smith-Njigba at 21.4 is the other way it goes wrong.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Footballers claim a quarterback at 07:00 Wednesday. They hold priority 8 and Bo Nix, Kyler Murray, Tyler Shough, Jordan Love, Bryce Young and Baker Mayfield all clear at the same moment. Any of those turns a 0.0 into roughly 16 and the 62% becomes a coin flip.

tonight.caseSources: ESPN league file · NFL.com · Yahoo Sports

doFirst.title: Claim Brock Purdy, drop Kyle Pitts
doFirst.subtitle: Three of the ten teams in this league carry exactly one quarterback and all three are hurt. One of them is your opponent this week. File this one FIRST.

case.label: Why the price is zero
case.body: Chem resets waiver priority every week, so a claim costs you nothing that carries. You are 2nd of 10. This is the league where speculative claims are free, and STRATEGY section 6 says to be aggressive here for exactly this reason.

case.label: The three broken quarterbacks
case.body: Bok-aneers start Jaxson Dart, who hurt his knee on the opening drive Monday. NFL Network reported on Tuesday that his MRI came back worse than the initial MCL read and that he may need season-ending surgery. Footballers start Caleb Williams, who Ben Johnson said will not practice this week. Nicky Jam start Jayden Daniels, whose left elbow dislocated for the second time in two years; Washington named Marcus Mariota the starter and expect him to hold the job beyond Week 3. All three roster no backup.

case.label: What Purdy actually is here
case.body: He is not your starter — Josh Allen projects 23.8 and is untouchable. Purdy is 90.2% rostered nationally, unowned here, 2-0, and ranked QB3. He is trade inventory against three desperate teams and a denial play against the one you play Sunday.

case.label: Why Pitts is the seat, against a 92.7% market
case.body: Dropping a player rostered in nine of ten leagues needs a reason on the record, and the reason is not the quarterback. Michael Penix Jr. was confirmed as Atlanta's Week 3 starter this morning and again this afternoon, a full participant with the knee, with Tua second and Cooper Rush third. It does not matter. Pitts played 26 of Atlanta's 69 offensive snaps in Week 2 — 38%, FEWER than backup tight ends Charlie Woerner (33) and Austin Hooper (30) — and turned it into one catch for 15 yards. He has one catch on four targets all season. The reason to move him is that he is not playing. The structural point, that Chem's RB/WR flex can never take a second tight end, is deliberately the secondary argument here: this brief once dropped Isaiah Likely on that reasoning alone and he scored 16.9 while the tight end it kept scored 0.0.

case.label: Why not Brian Thomas Jr. instead
case.body: This morning's brief ranked Thomas as the next seat to spend after Pitts, on a 74% route share. Fantasy Life's 21 September report also says Thomas and Jakobi Meyers were both managing injuries during Week 2, which is the stated reason Parker Washington's share spiked. That makes the 74% partly injury-suppressed and makes Thomas a worse drop than he looked at 07:15, not a better one. Pitts at 38% of snaps behind two backups is the cleaner cut.

case.label: You probably only win one contested claim
case.body: Stated because it changes the order. A successful claim is believed to send you to the back of the order for the rest of this waiver run, so plan on winning one contested claim tomorrow rather than two. That is why Purdy goes first: he is the one three other managers want. The Vikings defence below is 10.8% rostered and almost certainly uncontested, so it should still land behind him. If you would rather have the certain 1.7 points than the asset, reverse them — but do not assume both are safe.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Guillo-tinas, who hold priority 1, file on Purdy as a block — they already carry Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes and have no need, so it would be pure denial. Or all three quarterback-poor teams settle for Nix, Murray, Shough, Love, Young, Stroud or Darnold, all of which clear at the same moment, in which case nobody has to pay and Purdy is a dead bench seat you drop next week. Or Penix throws for 300 on Thursday and Pitts finally plays, which would say the 38% snap share was the injury week and not the role.

doFirst.title: Claim the Vikings D/ST, drop the Ravens
doFirst.subtitle: This replaces the Lions claim I told you to file this morning — wrong defence, and it hedged against your own receiver. File it SECOND, behind Purdy.

case.label: Why Baltimore has to go
case.body: Baltimore play Dallas with a 52.5 point total — the highest of all sixteen Week 3 games on the bet365 board as of 21 September, against a board median near 44. Baltimore are only -2.5, which implies Dallas at roughly 25. That is the worst environment you can hand a defence. Draft Sharks rank the Ravens 25th this week.

case.label: Why Minnesota and not Detroit
case.body: Draft Sharks rank Minnesota 4th and Detroit 11th. Minnesota held Chicago to three points in Week 2, blitzing on roughly three-quarters of dropbacks and pressuring on half of them. Tampa Bay are implied at about 22.5 in a 43.5-total game. The Lions card this morning also hedged your own starting receiver — Garrett Wilson is a Jet, and Detroit succeeding means Wilson failing. Minnesota has no such conflict.

case.label: The churn question, answered rather than dodged
case.body: This seat changed hands on 16 September, six days ago, which is inside the seven-day window STRATEGY section 3 closes. I am overriding it because section 5 says kicker and D/ST are streamed on matchup every week without sentiment, and because the gap is not marginal — 4th against 25th, and the week's highest total against a middling one. A 0.3-point stream would not clear this bar. This one does.

case.label: Why nobody outbids you
case.body: Minnesota are 10.8% rostered here and the band is RISER, not OWNED. Detroit at 51.4% is the defence the rest of the league is looking at.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Minnesota lose their pass rush on Wednesday's first Week 3 injury report, which does not exist yet for anyone outside Atlanta and Green Bay. Or Baltimore's 52.5 collapses on Dallas offensive injury news, which would partly rehabilitate the Ravens — and would simultaneously undercut the Tyler Loop hold below, since both rest on the same total. Closes wrong if Baltimore out-score Minnesota in Week 3 fantasy points.

doFirst.title: Move Jalen Coker into the flex over Terry McLaurin
doFirst.subtitle: Second day I have written this card. McLaurin still holds the flex slot in the 21:52 file. It costs nothing and the case got stronger today.

case.label: What changed since this morning
case.body: Two things, both confirmations rather than new guesses. The Washington Post and ProFootballRumors both named Marcus Mariota the Week 3 starter on 21 September. And Jayden Daniels' elbow is his second dislocation in two years; he saw specialists Tuesday and Wednesday, Washington have not placed him on IR, and Mariota is expected to hold the job at least one week beyond this one. In 2025 Daniels missed three games with a similar injury.

case.label: The matchup, which is the part a projection hides
case.body: Seattle have allowed the fewest fantasy points to receivers of any defence in the league through two games — eleven, total. That is the single toughest receiver draw on the board, and McLaurin draws it with a backup quarterback in a game where Washington are implied at roughly 17.5, among the lowest totals of the week. McLaurin's volume with Mariota is genuinely there — a 27.8% target share in Week 2 — but it converted at a 30.8% catch rate, the worst in the NFL among players with ten or more targets, and two catches on nine targets at Dallas.

case.label: What Coker actually is
case.body: Not a projection story. A 90% route share, 18th in the NFL, and a 29% target share, 8th. He played 57 of 61 snaps in Week 1 (93%) and has 16 catches on 18 targets across two games — an 88.9% catch rate — with two touchdowns, on a new three-year $35M deal. Eight catches in each of his first two games, the first Panther ever to do that to open a season. Bryce Young is healthy and went 23 of 36 for 287 and three scores in Week 2. Cleveland have allowed the 5th-most fantasy points to receivers.

case.label: The contested read
case.body: Two arguments against, both real. Dave Canales said on 19 September that 'there's no secret our offense in the pass game runs through TMac' — the head coach names Tetairoa McMillan, not Coker, and McMillan went 5 for 101 in Week 2. And Dan Quinn says Washington's playbook does not shrink for Mariota: 'what do you wanna feature with Marcus that you didn't with Jayden?' If you believe target share is the durable signal, McLaurin is the hold. I side with Coker because a 93% snap share and an 88.9% catch rate are the same volume signal with the efficiency attached, and because Carolina at Cleveland — despite carrying the lowest total on the board at 40.5 — still implies more offence than Washington's 17.5.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Washington name a starter other than Mariota, or Daniels returns inside two weeks after the specialist consultations. Or Cleveland hold Coker under five targets while Mariota still targets McLaurin eight or more times, which would say the route-share instrument beats the quarterback change and the flex goes back.

action.label: Coker into the flex · McLaurin out

whatWentWrong.title: I told you to claim the Lions D/ST this morning. Wrong defence.
whatWentWrong.lead: Draft Sharks have Detroit 11th and Minnesota 4th, and the Lions claim hedged Garrett Wilson — your own starting receiver — against your own defence.

case.label: What I got wrong
case.body: The 07:15 card priced the move on ESPN's projection alone: Detroit 7.8 against Baltimore's 6.0, net +1.8. That is a sort, not research. When I pulled an independent board this afternoon, Detroit sat 11th and Minnesota 4th.

case.label: The cost of the conflict
case.body: The morning card named the conflict honestly and took it anyway: Garrett Wilson is a Jet and starts for you. Detroit are -6.5 at home. A Lions defensive scoreline is a Wilson blank. There was never a reason to accept that when a conflict-free option ranked higher.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If Minnesota appear on Wednesday's injury report missing pass rushers, Detroit becomes the fallback rather than Jacksonville, whose 7.2 also beats Baltimore but re-adds a defence this roster dropped six days ago.

whatWentWrong.title: I nearly rewrote this morning's Pitts card on news it already had
whatWentWrong.lead: Atlanta naming Michael Penix Jr. is not new. The 07:15 brief had it, dismissed it, and made a better argument than the one I was about to make.

case.label: What I did wrong
case.body: I read this morning's published brief for its structure — section counts and card titles — and not for its contents, then started re-deriving the Pitts decision from scratch on this afternoon's search results. The runbook's rule is to read the existing file before overwriting it, and reading its shape is not reading it. The mistake cost nothing because it was caught before publishing, but it is exactly the failure that once destroyed a good trade proposal.

case.label: What the morning brief already knew
case.body: That Penix is confirmed as Atlanta's Week 3 starter, a full participant with the knee, with Tua second and Cooper Rush third — and that it does not matter, because Pitts played 26 of 69 snaps in Week 2, fewer than backup tight ends Charlie Woerner and Austin Hooper, for one catch. That is a stronger reason to cut him than the structural one I was going to lead with, and it is now the lead block on the card above.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing to falsify — this is a process note. The concrete consequence is that the Pitts drop now rests on a 38% snap share rather than on a flex-eligibility rule, which is a better-evidenced position than the brief held twelve hours ago.

whatWentWrong.title: Terry McLaurin draws the toughest receiver matchup in the league and is still in your flex
whatWentWrong.lead: Seattle have allowed eleven fantasy points to receivers in two games. Nobody has allowed fewer.

case.label: The number
case.body: Through Week 2, Seattle rank 1st of 32 in fantasy points allowed to the position. McLaurin's nine targets at Dallas were real and his Week 1 route participation was the highest on Washington, but those targets now come from Marcus Mariota in a game where Washington are implied at about 17.5.

case.label: Why it is still sitting there
case.body: The swap was written this morning and has not been made. It costs nothing — no priority, no roster move, reversible every week. It is the cheapest point available to you this week and it is going unclaimed.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Washington naming someone other than Mariota, or Cleveland shutting Coker down while Mariota keeps feeding McLaurin. Either sends the flex back.

whatWentWrong.sources: footballdb · Washington Post · FOX Sports odds board

whatWentWrong.title: The reason I benched Brian Thomas Jr. was half an artefact
whatWentWrong.lead: His 74% route share is real. So is the fact that he was playing hurt when it was measured.

case.label: The correction
case.body: Fantasy Life's 21 September utilization report has Parker Washington at a 90% route share and a 38% target share, Jakobi Meyers 88%, Thomas 74%. The same article says Thomas and Meyers were both managing injuries during Week 2, which is the stated reason Washington's share spiked. I reported the ranking this morning without the caveat attached to it.

case.label: What it does not change
case.body: He stays benched. Jacksonville's rolling three-game target count is Washington 30, Thomas 13, Meyers 7, and Trevor Lawrence went 3 of 11 for 14 yards and an interception outside the numbers in Week 2 — which is where Thomas lives. New England have been stingy across the board, 11th against receivers.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Thomas clearing an 85% route share against New England, or Parker Washington's 38% target share regressing under 25% across two games. It is the second-highest share in the league on a two-game sample and is the likeliest thing here to be noise.

worthALook.name: Rashod Bateman
worthALook.lead: I told you to claim him on Saturday. The signal that justified it has reversed and I am pulling the card.

case.label: Why he was a card
case.body: Nine targets and 7 for 88 with a touchdown at New Orleans while Zay Flowers sat, with Baltimore also missing Ja'Kobi Lane (fractured wrist) and Devontez Walker. Ownership rose 8.02 in a day, the largest single move on the Chem board, and he surfaced in the MONEY band.

case.label: The number that killed it
case.body: In tonight's file his ownership change is minus 0.12 and his band has dropped from MONEY to OWNED. The market stopped buying. And the vacancy is closing: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Zay Flowers has a 'good shot' to play against Dallas as long as he progresses in practice this week. Flowers went 5 for 150 and a touchdown in the first half of Week 1 before the hamstring, so his return does not leave Bateman much.

case.label: The seat problem
case.body: His only drop candidate was Kyle Pitts, and Purdy takes that seat tonight. Dropping a second body for a 7.6-point projection to chase a signal that has already turned is the churn STRATEGY section 3 exists to stop.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Wednesday's practice report is the first real signal and it lands after waivers process, which is the whole problem with claiming him tonight. If Flowers is limited or out again and Bateman clears unclaimed, he is a free agent and costs nothing at all. Waiting dominates claiming in every branch from here.

worthALook.sources: ESPN league file · NFL Network via The Big Lead · Baltimore Ravens

worthALook.name: Xavier Worthy
worthALook.lead: Leads all Kansas City receivers in snaps and is somehow free in a ten-team league.

case.label: The ownership anomaly
case.body: 74.7% rostered nationally and unowned here. STRATEGY section 4 calls this the strongest single wire signal in a shallow league — it usually means a manager blundered rather than that the player is bad.

case.label: The reason to wait anyway
case.body: Week 2 snap counts have Worthy at 69 (86%), ahead of Travis Kelce at 68 and Rashee Rice at 63. But he dropped two passes and the production went elsewhere: Kelce 9 of 11 for 101, Tyquan Thornton 4 for 86. Snaps without targets is a role waiting to convert, not one that has.

case.label: Where he would go
case.body: Nowhere, today. Jefferson, Wilson and Coker occupy the receiver and flex slots and none of them is losing his seat to a player whose last game was two drops.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Kansas City's air-yards distribution normalises across two weeks, or if Rice misses time. Rice is entirely off Kansas City's injury report, so that branch is closed for now.

worthALook.sources: AtoZ Sports · Arrowhead Pride via Yahoo · SI

worthALook.name: Adonai Mitchell
worthALook.lead: He out-targeted your own starting receiver on the same team last week, and five in six leagues have not noticed.

case.label: The observation
case.body: In Week 2 Mitchell led the Jets with a 32% target share and a 28% target-per-route-run rate, ahead of Garrett Wilson's 21% and 16% on similar route volume. That is the shape the runbook calls a player whose number has not caught up to his role: he projects 10.7 and is rostered in one league in six. Carried forward from this morning unchanged, because nothing today touched it.

case.label: Why it is a row and not a card
case.body: One week, and the claim is already spoken for. Wilson still runs 88% of the Jets' routes, New York are implied at only 20.5 against Detroit, and you realistically land one contested claim tomorrow. Buying the second receiver on a low-total offence is not what that claim is for.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Mitchell clearing a 25% target share again at Detroit. Two weeks makes it a role rather than a game script, and at that point he is the claim and Brian Thomas Jr. is the drop.

worthALook.sources: Draft Sharks · ESPN league file · carried from the 22 September 07:15 brief

doNotChase.name: Mark Andrews
doNotChase.lead: 82.2% rostered and free here, and still wrong for this roster specifically.

case.label: Why he keeps surfacing
case.body: 82.2% national ownership with availability in a ten-team league is a genuine OWNED anomaly, which is why he was a Do-first card for four consecutive runs before being demoted.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Six catches on seven targets for 49 and no score in Week 2, in the same game Rashod Bateman drew nine targets. He is no longer Baltimore's first read at his own position group.

case.label: The structural kill
case.body: Chem's flex is RB/WR only. Behind a healthy Isaiah Likely, Andrews has no lineup path in any week. Tonight's card is already spending the second tight-end seat, not filling it again.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Isaiah Likely appearing on a Giants injury report, which makes a second startable tight end necessary rather than dead weight. He is not on one this week, checked tonight.

doNotChase.sources: ESPN league file · Draft Sharks · Giants.com

doNotChase.name: Jakobi Meyers
doNotChase.lead: Plays nearly every snap Jacksonville runs and cannot get the ball thrown to him.

case.label: Why he looks like a buy
case.body: 76.2% rostered nationally, free here, and he played 53 snaps in Week 2 — 90% of Jacksonville's offensive plays. On snaps alone he is the Jaguars' most-used receiver.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: One catch for 28 yards on those 53 snaps. Jacksonville's rolling three-game target count is Parker Washington 30, Brian Thomas Jr. 13, Meyers 7. Snap share is not opportunity when the quarterback is not looking; SI's 21 September piece is literally headlined around why he must get more involved.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Meyers clearing eight targets against New England while Washington's 38% share regresses. That is the same clause that would rehabilitate Thomas, and both cannot be true at once.

doNotChase.sources: SI · Fantasy Life · ESPN league file

doNotChase.name: Eddy Pineiro
doNotChase.lead: The required kicker comparison, and the answer is hold Tyler Loop.

case.label: The comparison, reported rather than omitted
case.body: Best available on the Chem wire by ESPN projection: Pineiro 9.4, Trey Smack 8.7, Daniel Carlson 8.4, Tyler Bass 8.2. Loop is 8.2. On the raw number Pineiro is +1.2, which clears STRATEGY's one-point floor.

case.label: Why it is still a hold
case.body: Loop kicks in Baltimore at Dallas, the highest total of all sixteen Week 3 games at 52.5, with Baltimore implied at roughly 27.5. Brandon Aubrey, kicking in that same stadium, is the consensus K1 of the week — a board that ranks the opposing kicker first is a board expecting points there. The ESPN number and the betting market disagree and I take the market on kickers, because kicker scoring is almost entirely a function of how many times his offence reaches field-goal range.

case.label: The honest gap
case.body: I could not retrieve Draft Sharks' full Week 3 kicker board this run — only the top 25 rows loaded and Loop was not among them. So this comparison rests on ESPN projections plus the betting total, not on an independent kicker ranking. That is weaker evidence than I would like for a decision I am declining to make.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loop finishing outside the top twenty again in Week 3 while Pineiro or Carlson finish top five, or a top-five Week 4 kicker reaching genuine free agency in Chem, at which point the swap is costless and happens the same hour.

settled.title: Do not sell Terry McLaurin (15 September)
settled.result: Superseded rather than broken. The route-participation read was correct and his nine targets at Dallas vindicated it. What changed is the quarterback: those targets now come from Marcus Mariota. He stays on the roster; he comes out of the flex.

settled.title: Bench Brian Thomas Jr. because he is third in route share (this morning)
settled.result: Half right. The 74% is accurate, but the same Fantasy Life report says he and Meyers were both playing hurt when it was measured, and I reported the ranking without that caveat. He stays benched on the target counts, not on the route share.

settled.title: Decline Xavier Worthy despite the ownership anomaly (19 September)
settled.result: Held. He led Kansas City receivers in Week 2 snaps at 86% but dropped two passes, and the targets went to Kelce and Thornton. Carried here so the anomaly is not rediscovered next run as a find.

settled.title: Validate with the repo's validate.py rather than the runbook's inline copy (22 September)
settled.result: Now moot in the right direction. The runbook's Step 7 has been edited to fetch validate.py from the repo instead of embedding a copy, and the repo file reports 25 rules tonight. The KNOWN LIMITATIONS section has not been corrected on season projections — see the entry above.

settled.result: Read tonight. Chem is full PPR, scoring 1, flex slot 3 is RB/WR only, waiver priority resets weekly. Fourteen scoring items still differ from IPADE, so no number crosses between the two briefs.

settled.title: Cross-check every source against its date (20 September, standing rule)
settled.result: Earned its keep tonight. Two separate Brock Purdy 'will sit Week 3' stories surfaced at the top of search — both about turf toe, both from September 2025, one from Yahoo and one from CBS. Either would have killed the headline card on this brief. Neither is current.

cannotSee.label: Brock Purdy's current injury status
cannotSee.body: I could not retrieve a single September 2026 source explicitly confirming Purdy is healthy. What I have is indirect: the league file prices him at 21.0 with a 286.0 season projection and QB3 rank, his ownership is flat at 90.2%, and 2026-dated San Francisco coverage describes a 2-0 team without mentioning his availability. The direct searches returned 2025 turf-toe stories. The runbook warns that proj is not zeroed for unavailable players, so the projection is not proof.

cannotSee.label: Wednesday's injury reports
cannotSee.body: Only Atlanta and Green Bay have published Week 3 practice reports, because they play Thursday. Every other team's first report lands Wednesday, after waivers have already processed. Tonight's claims are being made one day before the information that would confirm them.

cannotSee.label: Zay Flowers' Week 3 status
cannotSee.body: Unresolved, and it decides whether Rashod Bateman is a real asset or a one-week artefact. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Flowers has a 'good shot' to play against Dallas as long as he progresses in practice this week — and that practice report lands Wednesday, after waivers have already processed.

cannotSee.label: Whether Jameis Winston is formally the Giants' starter
cannotSee.body: NFL.com reported on 22 September that Winston 'will likely start'. Giants.com the same day quotes the head coach saying evaluations are ongoing with no final decision. Two sources, same day, different answers. Isaiah Likely's projection assumes somebody competent throws.

cannotSee.label: Week 2's fantasy scores
cannotSee.body: The file only carries the current scoring period, so every actual is null and Week 2's results are gone. Everything in the settled list above is reconstructed from the decision log and from reporting, not from the file.

cannotSee.label: Malik Nabers' X-ray
cannotSee.body: He dislocated his shoulder on Monday, popped it back in himself, returned to the game and said postgame he would get an X-ray. No result published. If he misses time, Likely's route share climbs; if he is fine, the original Likely thesis keeps its live clause.

cannotSee.label: How much the matchup grades are worth
cannotSee.body: Every grade on the roster above comes from a two-game sample — footballdb's 2026 points-allowed table, complete through Week 2. At n=2 one blowout moves a defence ten places. They are tiebreakers. The table is also standard scoring, not PPR, which understates pass-catching backs and slot receivers.
